housing.summary: Vantaa is part of the Greater Helsinki metropolitan area and home to Helsinki Airport, so rents sit below central Helsinki but above the national average. Furnished and unfurnished one-bedroom flats are common near rail hubs like Tikkurila and Myyrmaki. Long-term leases usually run 12 months and most listings are in Finnish; a Finnish personal identity code and proof of income are typically expected before a landlord will sign.

banking.summary: Opening a Finnish bank account requires a residence permit (for non-EU citizens), a Finnish personal identity code, and identity documents. Banks apply strong identity verification and may take extra time for newcomers before granting online banking credentials, which double as a widely used e-identification tool. Major retail banks operate branches across the Helsinki region including Vantaa.

schools.summary: Public comprehensive education follows the Finnish national curriculum and is free. Vantaa offers Finnish- and Swedish-language schools plus English-medium and international options within commuting distance in the Helsinki region, including IB programmes. Early childhood education (varhaiskasvatus) is subsidised and income-based.

legal_admin.summary: New residents register with the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) to obtain a Finnish personal identity code and register their municipality of residence. EU/EEA citizens staying over three months register their right of residence with Finnish Immigration Service; non-EU nationals need a residence permit first. The personal identity code unlocks banking, healthcare and tax services.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with DVV to receive a Finnish personal identity code and register municipality of residence

tax_finance.summary: Anyone working in Finland must obtain a tax card (verokortti) from the Finnish Tax Administration (Vero), which sets the withholding rate applied by employers. Newcomers request a tax card in person or online once they hold a personal identity code. Finland taxes worldwide income for tax residents; short-term workers may fall under a flat tax-at-source scheme.

transport.summary: Vantaa is served by HSL (Helsinki Region Transport), covering buses, trams, metro, commuter trains and the Ring Rail Line connecting the city and Helsinki Airport. A single regional ticket works across all modes, and monthly season tickets are zone-based. Public transport is extensive, reducing the need for a car.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences are valid as-is; non-EU/EEA licences may be exchanged or must be re-taken depending on the country of issue and residency length
transport.healthcare_registration: Register for public healthcare via the wellbeing services county and Kela (social insurance) after obtaining a personal identity code
